title: Candidate benchmark scan for the transfer setting (evolve on one, evaluate on the rest) with a headroom pilot on 5 training-split candidates
purpose: Purpose 2. The metric is generalisation: evolve a Skill on ONE benchmark and evaluate it on the OTHERS, choosing benchmarks where a gain can actually be measured. The scan says which public benchmarks could join or replace the current five, and the headroom pilot shows where text instructions move deepseek-v4-flash's score, which is where a learned Skill could show a measurable transfer effect.
verdict_cn:
E3 结论：为"在一个基准上进化、在其余基准上评测"（目的 2：泛化性）挑选候选基准。"基准"就是一套公开的标准题库加评分方法。

一、做了什么
1. 把六类公开基准（检索问答、文档/表格问答、数学、编程、具身智能体、电子表格）共约 40 个候选逐一核对：许可证、题目数量、两台机器上有没有现成数据、写评分程序要花多少工夫、求解模型会不会"提前见过"这些题（数据污染），以及哪些基准之间可能互相迁移。
2. 做了"提升空间扫描"小实验，只用训练集题目。在新机器上用求解模型 deepseek-v4-flash，对 5 个基准各抽 80 题，每题跑 2 遍。这 5 个是：HotpotQA（多跳问答）、TAT-QA（财报表格问答）、FinQA（财报计算题）、MATH（竞赛数学最难一级）、MBPP（基础 Python 编程）。比较三种提示：
   - 什么都不加（NoSkill）；
   - 由公开任务说明卡改写的指令（card，和项目里 I-ds 种子的做法相同）；
   - 我按任务描述手写的专家技能（expert，没看任何数据）。
   另外把现有五个基准的说明文字原样套到相似的新基准上，测"直接迁移"。还做了"污染探测"：不给文档直接提问，或者给题目的前半段，看模型能不能背出后半段。
3. 总共用了约 343 万 token（模型处理文字的计量单位），在 400 万的预算内。

二、主要发现
1. 只看"答案内容对不对"（不计格式）时，在说明卡之上再加专家技能，五个基准的变化都在正负 4 分以内，统计上都不显著。说明卡比"什么都不加"显著更好的只有 HotpotQA（+6 分）和 FinQA（+4 分）。这和项目之前的结论一致：在好的说明之上，学到的条款只多 3～5 分，而且不显著。
2. 24～36 分的大幅涨跌，几乎都来自"答案格式约定"：数学题有没有把答案放进规定的标签；TAT-QA 有没有写出"千、百万、%"等单位；FinQA 有没有带百分号。我手写技能里一句含糊的格式话，就让 FinQA 的 42 道百分比题全部判错（-40 分），可算出来的数其实是对的。这类约定能从训练中的失败里学到，但每个评分程序的约定都不一样。
3. 把现有基准的说明文字直接套到"话题相似"的新基准上，五个全部掉分（17～54 分）。数学连内容也掉了 26 分：选择题的做法害了要自己算答案的数学题。编程掉了 54 分：模型改去写读写 Excel 文件的程序。所以"话题相似"不等于"能迁移"。评测迁移时，要拿"目标基准自己的说明卡 + 迁移过来的规则"去和"只有目标说明卡"比，不能用源基准的文字把目标的说明换掉。
4. 测量精度：
   - 问答和表格类基准加上说明卡后，同一提示跑两遍，只有 2～5/80 题的结果会变（v3 的 SearchQA 是 15.5%）。
   - 每题的花费只有 OfficeQA 的 1/3～1/5、ALFWorld 的 1/15～1/60，同样的预算能用多得多的题。
   - HotpotQA 大约 70 道配对题就能测出 5 分的差异。
   - 数学题跑两遍有 21～26% 的题结果会变，不适合用来测量。
   - MBPP 不加提示已经 91% 正确，GSM8K（小学数学应用题）87%，几乎没有提升空间。
5. 污染探测：
   - 不给文档时，FinQA 和 TAT-QA 几乎答不出（约 1%），说明模型没有背答案。
   - HotpotQA 不给段落也能答对 32%，靠的是百科常识。
   - MATH 有 10～15% 的题，模型能逐字背出后半段，有记忆的迹象。

三、建议
1. 如果要换基准来争取"能测出来的提升"，证据最好的组合是"多跳问答一家"：在 HotpotQA 上进化，在 2WikiMultihopQA、MuSiQue、SearchQA 上评测。这四个用同一种"精确匹配"评分，格式约定一致。
2. 可以再加"财报表格一家"：在 TAT-QA 上进化，在 FinQA、OfficeQA 上评测，专门检验"在相似目标上不掉分"。
3. 不要用 MATH、MBPP、GSM8K 当进化的来源。
4. 要实话实说：内容上能提升的空间大约只有 2～4 分，光换成经典基准并不能保证出现显著提升。可行性：中等。工程上容易，但效果是否存在还不确定。

evidence:
All [measured] on 80 TRAINING items per candidate, 2 runs (neighbor arm 1 run), deepseek-v4-flash at temperature 0 with thinking disabled. "content" = lenient scorer plus fallback extraction (format-free). Strict / content accuracy for NoSkill, card, expert:
- HotpotQA-hard: .581/.713, .700/.775, .719/.794
- TAT-QA: .494/.856, .456/.812, .731/.850
- FinQA: .625/.744, .700/.787, .294/.787
- MATH L5: .356/.756, .719/.806, .669/.769
- MBPP: .906, .906, .912
- Side probes: GSM8K NoSkill 52/60; NQ-open closed-book 11/60 (49/60 dead).

Paired contrasts:
- card - NoSkill, content: HotpotQA +0.062 [+0.025,+0.106] (9 up/0 down, p=.004); FinQA +0.044 [0,+0.094] (8/1, p=.039); MATH +0.050 n.s.; TAT-QA -0.044 n.s.; MBPP 0.
- expert - card, content: -0.037 to +0.037 on all five (p >= .29).
- Strict-only effects: MATH card - NoSkill +0.362 (43/6; NoSkill omitted the answer tag in 40/80 and 43/80 replies). TAT-QA expert - card +0.275 (26/3; scale-word items 0/22 -> 14/22 and 26/62 -> 52/62). FinQA expert - card -0.406 (3/37; percentage items 67/84 -> 0/84 because the expert text made the model drop "%").
- Neighbor (v3 seed of the nearest current benchmark, unscoped) vs the target card, strict: HotpotQA -0.200, TAT-QA -0.194, FinQA -0.412, MATH -0.169, MBPP -0.544. Content: MATH -0.256 (5/28, p<.001), FinQA -0.062 (0/7, p=.016), MBPP -0.544, HotpotQA -0.037 n.s., TAT-QA 0.000.

Noise (strict flips between two identical runs, NoSkill/card/expert, of 80): HotpotQA 13/2/3; TAT-QA 5/5/3; FinQA 2/4/1; MATH 17/21/17; MBPP 3/1/4. For comparison, v3 SearchQA moved 30/194.

Dead/always-pass/movable items (strict): HotpotQA 21/38/21; TAT-QA 15/27/38; FinQA 19/17/44; MATH 7/16/57; MBPP 5/67/8.

Items needed for a 5-point paired effect: HotpotQA 68 (SD .147); MBPP 69; MATH 424; TAT-QA/FinQA 666/905 (SD inflated by the format effect).

Contamination probe (closed book): FinQA 1/80, TAT-QA 1/79, HotpotQA 25/78. Verbatim continuation of >= 8 words: MATH 6/40 (ROUGE-L >= .8 on 4/40), GSM8K 2/40, MBPP 1/39.

Delivery: 2,934/2,960 pilot cells delivered; 26 failures (15 http_429, 11 truncations) were counted as fails.

Cost per cell: HotpotQA 1.4-1.8k tokens, TAT-QA 0.6-1.2k, FinQA 1.1-1.9k, MBPP 0.2-0.6k. v3 training cells: OfficeQA 4.7-7.9k, ALFWorld 28-106k.

[verified] Locally available: the E3 train downloads, BigCodeBench v0.1.4 (both machines; evaluation image loaded only on the old machine), DocVQA id split (old machine), ALFWorld and the current pools. The HF caches hold models only.
design:
Proposed benchmark design for purpose 2 [estimate, grounded in the pilot]:
- Family A (shared output contract; small but measurable effects): evolve on HotpotQA distractor-hard (train 90,447; card arm flips 2/80; about 68 paired items per 5-point effect). Similar targets: 2WikiMultihopQA (Apache-2.0), MuSiQue-answerable (CC BY 4.0), and SearchQA (current). All score short spans with SQuAD exact match over supplied paragraphs.
- Family B (large learnable conventions; a real 'no drop on similar targets' check): evolve on TAT-QA (train 13,251 questions). Targets: FinQA (train 6,251) and OfficeQA. Conventions differ: TAT-QA wants scale words, FinQA wants % and no scale.
- Dissimilar controls: MATH or MBPP (expect no change; a drop counts as negative transfer).
- Transfer contrast: target(card + transferred rules, placed in a scoped section with an applicability condition) vs target(card) alone, on the target's own scorer, same items, >= 2 runs, >= 100 items per target. Never use the source text as a replacement for the target card: the neighbor probe shows -17 to -54 points from that.
- Report strict AND content scores, so format conventions are not reported as learned reasoning.
- Pre-flight per benchmark before admission:
  1. Check that the card matches the scorer's conventions (the GLM-written TAT-QA card garbled the scale rule and scored below NoSkill).
  2. Run a NoSkill/card/expert headroom scan like this one.
  3. Measure 2-run noise.
  4. Run closed-book/continuation contamination probes.
- Exclude as evolve sources: MATH (21-26% flips, verbatim recall on 10-15% of items); MBPP and GSM8K (ceiling); NQ-open closed-book (knowledge-bound); benchmarks without a train split (FRAMES, BrowseComp(-Plus), MATH-500, AIME, HumanEval(+), LiveCodeBench), which can only be targets.

pilot.result:
Headroom scan: 5 candidates x 80 training items x 3 arms x 2 runs, plus a neighbor transfer arm (1 run) and GSM8K/NQ-open side probes. 2,920 scan cells + 40 smoke cells; 3,378,949 solver tokens + 4,268 GLM + 50,721 probe tokens.

Where instructions move the score most:
- Strict, convention-sensitive scorers: MATH card vs NoSkill +36.2 points (answer-tag compliance); TAT-QA expert vs card +27.5 (scale words); HotpotQA card vs NoSkill +11.9; FinQA expert -40.6 (a self-inflicted % convention error).
- Content (format-free): only HotpotQA +6.2 (9/0, p=.004) and FinQA +4.4 (8/1, p=.039) for card vs NoSkill; expert vs card within +/-3.7 points everywhere, n.s.
- Unscoped transfer of the nearest current benchmark's seed lost 17-54 points strict on all five; content losses on MATH -25.6, MBPP -54.4, FinQA -6.2.

Candidate ranking for measurable transfer: HotpotQA family (low noise, shared scorer) > TAT-QA/FinQA (large but convention-bound effects) > MATH (noisy, memorised) > MBPP/GSM8K (ceiling).

This is a feasibility pilot, not a method result: one card and one expert text per benchmark, approximate (non-official) TAT-QA/FinQA scorers.

risks:
1. Small design: one expert author, one GLM card per benchmark, 80 items, 2 runs. The expert arm is not an upper bound; it contains a self-inflicted FinQA formatting error.
2. The strict scorers for TAT-QA/FinQA are my approximations, not the official scripts. Strict effect sizes depend on these conventions. The content score uses fallback heuristics (last line or last \boxed).
3. The neighbor arm is a single run and the unscoped worst case. Real Skills place rules under 'Applies when' sections, so its losses overstate what a gated learned rule would do; the positive-transfer side was not tested at all.
4. Contamination probes measure memorisation signals on training items only, with no post-cutoff control. The PJLAB route's DeepSeek snapshot is unknown (V4-Flash 2026-04-22 or later variants) and could change.
5. Content headroom over a good card is about 2-4 points. Even a well-chosen family may yield only a small, hard-to-detect transfer effect; swapping benchmarks alone does not guarantee a measurable gain.
6. Conventions conflict across 'similar' financial benchmarks, so a rule learned on TAT-QA may hurt FinQA/OfficeQA unless it is gated.
7. Licence caveats: SpreadsheetBench has no GitHub LICENSE; MultiHiertt and LiveMathematicianBench licences were not found; SheetCopilot is GPL; MathArena 2026 sets are CC BY-NC-SA (non-commercial); OfficeQA and GPQA are gated.
8. The deepseek route was congested at times (431 of 2,960 pilot cells needed retries; 15 http_429 failures).
cost_estimate:
This exploration: about 3.43M tokens (solver 3,378,949; GLM 4,268; probe 50,721), within the 4M budget.

Next pilot, prepared but not run [estimate]: card vs card+rule on 100 items each of HotpotQA, 2Wiki, MuSiQue and SearchQA x 2 runs, about 1,600 cells x ~1.8k tokens, roughly 2.9M tokens. Plus downloading the 2Wiki and MuSiQue train splits (free) and 1-2 days of harness work (EM/F1 scorer and backend wiring for two short-answer QA benchmarks).

Full family-A or family-B chain under the coevo5 protocol [estimate]: per step about 0.7M tokens of training cells (200 items x 2 runs x 1.8k) plus gate rounds of roughly 2-5M. That is roughly 3-6M per step, about 3-10x cheaper than v3's OfficeQA/ALFWorld stages per item.

Engineering estimates: TAT-QA/FinQA official-style scorers 1-2 days; DocVQA (OCR + ANLS), HumanEval+/MBPP+ and WikiTQ 2-5 days each; FRAMES, BrowseComp(-Plus), LiveCodeBench, WebShop, ScienceWorld, TextWorld and SheetCopilot 1-2+ weeks each.
recommendation:
1. Purpose 2: if the owner wants benchmarks where 'evolve on one, evaluate on the rest' can show a measurable gain, use a shared-scorer multi-hop QA family. Evolve on HotpotQA; evaluate on 2WikiMultihopQA, MuSiQue and SearchQA; keep MATH or MBPP as dissimilar controls. Optionally add the financial-table family (evolve on TAT-QA; evaluate on FinQA and OfficeQA) as the explicit 'no drop on similar targets' test.
2. Be honest up front: content-level headroom over a good task card is about 2-4 points on every candidate. Classic benchmarks alone will not produce a large learned-Skill gain. The large score swings are answer-format conventions and must be reported separately (strict vs content).
3. Measure transfer as target(card + transferred rules) vs target(card); never let source text replace the target card (-17 to -54 points in the pilot).
4. Before admitting any benchmark, run this pre-flight: a card-vs-scorer convention check, a NoSkill/card/expert headroom scan, 2-run noise, and closed-book/continuation contamination probes.
5. Do not use MATH, MBPP, GSM8K or closed-book NQ as evolve sources. Benchmarks without a train split (FRAMES, BrowseComp(-Plus), MATH-500, AIME, HumanEval(+), LiveCodeBench) can only be targets.
6. Next step: the ~2.9M-token family-A pilot (card vs card + one learned or hand-written rule on 4 x 100 items x 2 runs). Cross-reference D5/D8 (power), D9 (headroom), D12 (transfer measurement) and D6 (TextWorld as a generator of tasks with guaranteed answers).
